title: Telefónica / O2
description: Led product and service design across 5 locations for Telefonica's global health and digital portfolio. Delivered a chronic disease service reducing mortality by 48%, Parkinson's voice detection at 78% precision, and pandemic prediction tools with WHO and Harvard.

sections.title: Context
sections.body: Telefonica is one of the world's largest telecoms operators, with major consumer brands including O2 (UK), Movistar (Spain and Latin America), and Vivo (Brazil). Over five years, I led UX, product, and service design teams across 5 global locations, building a portfolio of eHealth, cloud, and data privacy products. Teams ranged from 10 to 17 people.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: Telefonica was investing in health and digital services as a strategic growth area adjacent to core telecoms. The challenge was demonstrating that a telecoms company could build products with genuine clinical and commercial value — not just technology prototypes. Each product area had a distinct business problem: chronic disease management had high healthcare costs and readmission rates; Parkinson's detection had no accessible early screening pathway; epidemic tracking had weeks-long detection lag times.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I personally led product and service design across the full portfolio. This included setting direction, leading user research programmes, designing clinical and consumer-facing product, managing cross-functional teams, and maintaining relationships with clinical and institutional partners (NHS, WHO, UNICEF, Harvard). Team management and budgeting were mine; technical implementation was delegated.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: Each product was grounded in field research before design began — home visits for chronic disease, clinical workflow research for Parkinson's, mobility data analysis for pandemic prediction. I ran co-design workshops with clinical staff, facilitated cross-functional delivery, and managed the tension between the pace of a commercial product team and the rigour required by clinical and regulatory partners. Across 20+ MVPs, the selection of which 5 to launch was driven by validated demand and commercial viability, not technical interest. Collaboration extended beyond healthcare: we worked with the elBulli Foundation, applying the Sapiens methodology to digital service design — a collaboration that also led to BulliPedia. One of the launched products was Radio.me, enabling elderly users to send and receive WhatsApp messages via voice call, with no smartphone required.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body: The portfolio demonstrated that a telecoms company could deliver genuine clinical and commercial impact. The chronic disease service reduced mortality by 48% and hospital readmissions by 63%. Parkinson's voice detection reached 78% precision. Of 20+ MVPs developed, five reached launch — each selected on validated demand, not technical ambition. Radio.me went on to serve elderly users across Spain, giving them access to WhatsApp without ever touching a smartphone.
